articles.title: Hawkish Fed repricing and Iran tensions trigger a major Bitcoin liquidation wave
articles.description: Bitcoin faced a big wave of liquidations over the past few days as the hawkish Fed repricing tightened financial conditions, weighing on the crypto market. The culprit was of course the very hawkish Fed’s Waller speech in which he also floated the idea of a larger 50 bps hike at the December meeting. His remarks triggered a strong hawkish repricing which was then exacerbated by the hotter than expected US CPI data. Moreover, Trump stated on Truth Social that the US doesn’t need a deal with Iran, triggering a rally in oil prices and weighing further on the risk sentiment. Looking ahead, Bitcoin will likely remain under pressure amid the negative macro backdrop. We will likely need a more dovish Fed or a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations to reverse the trend. BITCOIN TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME On the daily chart, we can see that Bitcoinerased all the gains since August after the more hawkish Fed stance and the hotter than expected US CPI data. The price bounced from the 62,000 support amid some profit-taking, but the macro backdrop remains negative. If we get a pullback into the 67,000 resistance, we can expect the sellers to step in, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting the 58,000 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the major downward trendline around the 75,000 level. ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 4 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. If we get a pullback into the trendline, we can expect the sellers to lean on it, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to increase the bullish bets into the major downward trendline next. ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 1 hour chart, we have some consolidation after the strong selloff. We have a swing low around the 63,750 level that could act as support. The buyers will likely step in there, with a defined risk below the level, to position for a pullback into the 67,000 resistance. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to pile in for a drop into the 62,000 support, targeting a break below it. The red lines define the average daily range for today. UPCOMING CATALYSTS Today we have Fed Chair Warsh speaking. Tomorrow, we get the US Retail Sales. On Wednesday, we have the FOMC meeting minutes. On Thursday, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on Fed speakers and the US-Iran stalemate. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

articles.title: ‘God Save the King!’: Lalit Modi reveals he has become a British citizen
articles.description: IPL founder Lalit Modi announces he has become a British citizen Citizenship ceremony took place in London in September Modi left India in 2010 amid allegations of financial irregularities He rejects being called a “fugitive”, saying he has not been convicted INDIAN PREMIER LEAGUE(IPL) founder Lalit Modi has announced that he has become a British citizen, describing the UK as his “home for many years”. Modi, who has lived in London for several years, shared the news on X on Saturday alongside photographs of his citizenship ceremony at a London town hall in September. He said he had chosen to make the “very special and personal milestone” public during an address at the Oxford Union. “I am proud to be a British citizen,” he wrote. “On 15 September 2026, surrounded by family and friends, I celebrated my British citizenship at a ceremony that will always hold a special place in my heart.” IPL: 5 criticisms levelled by Lalit Modi against BCCI on current format “The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply — its people, institutions, traditions and values,” he said, describing his citizenship as “a privilege and a responsibility”. His post ended with a reference to King Charles’s 78th birthday, which fell on the same day: “A particularly special day to share this moment. God Save the King!” Legal battles in India Modi left India in May 2010 after being suspended by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) amid allegations of financial irregularities in the IPL. In 2015, a special court issued a non-bailable warrant against him after he failed to respond to summonses from the Enforcement Directorate in a money laundering case. Vanuatu prime minister orders cancellation of Lalit Modi’s passport In July this year, an appellate tribunal set aside a penalty imposed on him in a separate case under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), relating to the IPL’s 2009 season in South Africa. Modi has strongly objected to being described as a “fugitive”, saying he has not been convicted of any criminal offence. (With inputs from PTI)
